## The Script Tax: Measuring Tokenization-Driven Efficiency and Latency Disparities

Pretrained multilingual language models are often assumed to be script-agnostic, yet their tokenizers can impose systematic costs on certain writing systems.

**Main Results:**

Across mBERT and XLM-R, the higher-fragmentation orthography shows a ~3.4x increase in fertility (6.73-6.85 vs. 2.10-2.35 tokens/word), leading to a 16.5x inference slowdown (0.23 vs. 3.8 sentences/second) on identical hardware.

**Conclusion:**

The results highlight tokenization as a key source of inequity in multilingual NLP and motivate script-aware tokenization and pretraining.

## Paper Overview

The paper addresses multilingual reasoning as a significant challenge for large language models (LLMs), with performance disproportionately favoring high-resource languages.

## Core Hypothesis and Methodology

The researchers hypothesize that, drawing inspiration from cognitive neuroscience which suggests human reasoning functions largely independently of language processing, LLMs similarly encode reasoning and language as separable components that can be disentangled to enhance multilingual reasoning. To evaluate this, they perform a causal intervention by ablating language-specific representations at inference time.

## Results

Experiments on 10 open-weight LLMs spanning 11 typologically diverse languages show that this language-specific ablation consistently boosts multilingual reasoning performance. Layer-wise analyses further confirm that language and reasoning representations can be effectively disentangled throughout the model, yielding improved multilingual reasoning capabilities, while preserving top-layer language features remains essential for maintaining linguistic fidelity.

## Advantages

Compared to post-training methods such as supervised fine-tuning or reinforcement learning, the training-free language-reasoning disentanglement achieves comparable or superior results with minimal computational overhead.

The paper was presented as a poster at NeurIPS 2025.
